name: Cape Cod National Seashore
blurb: Dunes, pine barrens and cold seas where seals draw in great white sharks.

tip.title: Remove the gray seals
tip.text: Seals eat sand lance and feed sharks and coyotes. Set Gray seal to -100% and watch the great white shark, the coyote and the gulls that scavenge them.

sources.title: NPS: Nature and science at Cape Cod National Seashore

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Drives growth of the dune plants, pines and the plankton of the bay and open ocean.
Cool, nutrient-bearing water around the outer Cape feeds plankton, which supports fish, seals and whales.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, shellfish and carcasses, returning nutrients to the sandy soil.
Microscopic algae that form the base of the marine food web off the Cape.
A dune grass whose spreading roots and stems trap blowing sand and help build and hold dunes.

nodes.name: Pitch pine
nodes.desc: A hardy pine of sandy, poor soils that dominates much of the Cape's pine barrens woodland.

nodes.name: Black cherry
nodes.desc: A common native tree and shrub of the Cape whose leaves and fruit are food for deer and small mammals.
Tiny planktonic crustaceans that graze on phytoplankton and feed small fish.
A filter-feeding mussel of rocky and sandy shores that strains plankton from the water.
Browses woody plants and fruit across the Cape's woods and heaths.
A small grassland rodent that eats plants and seeds and is prey for foxes and coyotes.
Eats conifer seeds and other plant foods; a common resident of the pine woods.
A sea duck that dives for mussels and other shellfish along the coast.
A baleen whale that feeds in nearby waters on schooling fish such as sand lance.

nodes.name: Great black-backed gull
nodes.desc: A large gull that eats shellfish and fish and scavenges carrion, including seal remains.
Preys on rodents, squirrels and birds, and also eats fruit.
Drawn to the Cape's seal colonies, where it hunts gray seals near shore.
The Cape's top land predator; eats deer, small mammals and carrion.
